title: Algebra
text: hermes.algebra Algebra A query is an immutable plan built one operator at a time. The explorer applies an action, runs the plan, and reports what changed. On this page Actions The explorer Observations Policies Actions Each action is a frozen dataclass with an apply(plan) method, written as one JSON object. parse_action turns the JSON into a typed command. Source: algebra.py . Action SPARQL algebra Example triple BGP, join {"op": "triple", "pattern": "?c ex:hosted ?g"} filter Filter {"op": "filter", "expr": "?year > 1900"} optional LeftJoin {"op": "optional", "patterns": ["?c ex:country ?k"]} union Union {"op": "union", "branches": [[...], [...]]} minus Minus {"op": "minus", "patterns": [...]} bind Extend {"op": "bind", "expr": "YEAR(?date)", "var": "?y"} group , aggregate Group, Aggregation {"op": "aggregate", "expr": "COUNT(?g)", "alias": "?n"} having Filter on groups {"op": "having", "expr": "?n > 2"} order OrderBy {"op": "order", "expr": "DESC(?n)"} project , distinct Project, Distinct {"op": "project", "vars": ["?c"]} limit , offset Slice {"op": "limit", "n": 1} ask ASK form {"op": "ask"} remove retract a triple or filter {"op": "remove", "text": "?c ex:country ?k"} Two actions read the graph and leave the plan alone: lookup finds entities whose label contains a text, and inspect lists the predicates around an entity, or used by the instances of a class, with counts and an example value. Control actions are goal (see Verifier ), undo , and finish . render(plan, header) is the builder from a plan to SPARQL. It is deterministic. The explorer from hermes.algebra import Explorer, parse_action explorer = Explorer(kg) explorer.run(parse_action({"op": "triple", "pattern": "?city ex:hosted ?g"})) explorer.preview(parse_action({"op": "triple", "pattern": "?g ex:season \"Winter\""})) print(explorer.sparql) run commits a plan-changing action only if the new plan parses, passes the verifier when one is installed, and runs. preview returns the same observation without committing. undo restores the previous plan. Explorer(kg, sample_size=5, kernel=None) ; pass a kernel to type-check every step. Observations After each step the explorer runs two queries: the number of solutions, as a COUNT over the plan used as a subquery, and a sample of rows under LIMIT . An ASK plan reports its Boolean. Observation.summary() is the line the planner reads: {"op": "triple", "pattern": "?city ex:hosted ?g"} -> 19 solutions {"op": "triple", "pattern": "?city ex:country ex:USA"} -> 19 -> 8 solutions {"op": "triple", "pattern": "?g ex:season \"Winter\""} -> 8 -> 4 solutions {"op": "distinct"} -> 4 -> 3 solutions A rejected step reads rejected: ... with the parser, verifier, or store message. Executions are memoized by the store cache. Policies Any policy can choose the actions. The algebra-agent system is an LLM policy: each turn it sees the action catalogue, the vocabulary, linked entities, every earlier action and observation, and the current query, and replies with one action. It stops on finish or after max_steps (15), refuses an action identical to the previous one, and returns the last committed plan that runs. Source: algebra_agent.py . UniQGen's Chase and Backchase is, in these terms, a beam search over remove and triple . Previous Playground Next Verifier

title: Benchmarks
text: hermes.benchmarks Benchmarks Every benchmark, whatever its source format, is stored the same way, so every system is scored the same way. On this page The suite Format Commands Caveats The suite Name Questions Items Graph License ck26 50 100 (en, de) Text2SPARQL corporate graph, local CC BY-SA 4.0 db26 50 100 (en, es) DBpedia, organizers' endpoint CC BY-SA 4.0 ck25 50 50 (en) corporate graph, local CC BY-SA 4.0 db25 100 200 (en, es) DBpedia, organizers' endpoint CC BY-SA 4.0 qald10 394 1,564 Wikidata, live MIT qald9plus 150 450 DBpedia, live CC BY 4.0 Format data/graphs.yaml local files or an endpoint per graph data/benchmarks/<name>/benchmark.yaml graph, languages, license, source URLs and SHA-256 data/benchmarks/<name>/questions.jsonl one row per question and language data/benchmarks/<name>/gold.json gold answer sets {"id": "ck26:7-en", "qid": "7", "lang": "en", "question": "...", "sparql": "...", "features": ["SELECT", "ORDER"], "order_matters": false} Ids follow the official scorer. Gold answers use its layout: every value of every variable, flattened into one set. Sources are pinned to commits. Adapters convert Text2SPARQL YAML and QALD JSON; a new benchmark is an adapter and an entry in sources.py . Source: benchmarks/ . Commands hermes data list # known and downloaded benchmarks hermes data fetch ck26 db26 # download, normalize, fetch local graphs hermes data verify ck26 # run every gold query and compare with gold Caveats Read first These facts change how any number on these benchmarks should be read. CK26 is CK25 paraphrased. 49 of the 50 CK26 gold queries appear verbatim in CK25, on the same graph. Neither is a development set for the other. Runs count overlapping few-shot examples as contaminated_examples . The CK gold answers depend on the engine. They were computed on Tentris. On Oxigraph, 43 of 50 CK26 gold queries reproduce; the rest differ in tie-breaking under LIMIT , number formatting, or the non-standard xsd:int() . All 50 DB26 gold queries reproduce on the organizers' endpoint. QALD answers drift. QALD-9-plus targets DBpedia 2016-10 and QALD-10 was answered on Wikidata in 2022; the live endpoints have changed. Previous Graph stores Next Leaderboard

title: Evaluation
text: hermes.evaluation Evaluation The scorer reproduces all 5,024 published Text2SPARQL 2026 scores, so Hermes numbers sit on the leaderboard's scale. On this page Metrics Parity Official quirks and the strict variant Reproducible subset Metrics The official scorer flattens every value of every variable into one set and scores it with trec_eval: set precision, set recall, and set F1 per question, nDCG where order matters, and the ranking metric set_F_ndcg , which uses nDCG on those questions and F1 elsewhere. score(result, gold, order_matters, strict) scores one question; aggregate(per_item, languages, strict) gives overall and per-language averages. Source: evaluation.py . Parity experiments/check_scorer.py downloads every team's predictions and official scores for CK26 and DB26 from the pinned challenge repository, rescores them, and compares all 5,024 per-question and average numbers. None differ. Official quirks and the strict variant Official behavior Strict An ASK answer is a document named true . A gold true scores 1.0 whatever the answer; a gold false scores 0.0 for everyone. Booleans score by exact match. nDCG ignores the returned order, since every value has the same score. nDCG uses the returned order. set_F_ndcg counts the scope's mean nDCG as one extra item. A plain mean. Runs report both, side by side. Reproducible subset Each run also reruns every gold query on its own store and flags gold_reproduces . The reproducible averages restrict the official metrics to those items, which separates a method's errors from differences between graph engines. Previous Leaderboard Next Experiments

title: Experiments
text: hermes.experiments, hermes.serve Experiments An experiment is a YAML config. A run predicts, executes, and scores every item, and keeps everything needed to reproduce or audit it. On this page Config A run Leaderboard Challenge API Rules for comparable numbers Config benchmark: ck26 system: uniqgen params: # constructor arguments of the system beam_width: 5 llm: provider: ollama # or openai model: llama3.1 cache: .cache/llm languages: [en] # optional limit: 20 # optional examples: # optional few-shot pool from another benchmark benchmark: db25 limit: 10 leak_gold: true # ablations only: gold answers in context.answers Configs live in configs/<benchmark>/ . bash experiments/run_all.sh reruns them all. A run hermes run configs/ck26/prover.yaml [--limit N] [--resume RUN_ID] For each item, the system predicts a query, the query runs on the benchmark's store, and the answers are scored. Errors are recorded, not raised. A run writes results/<benchmark>/<config>/<run id>/ : File Contents config.yaml the config as run predictions.jsonl per item: SPARQL, error, seconds, official and strict scores, gold_reproduces , and system traces metrics.json official , strict , and reproducible averages, error count, latency p50 and p95 run.json model, model calls and cache hits, graph executions, contaminated examples, the commit the run started from and whether src/ had local changes Observers receive start, item, and end events; Progress prints one line per item. Source: experiments.py . Leaderboard hermes report [--benchmark ck26] [--write] Prints the latest run of each config next to the official Text2SPARQL 2026 entries from results/peers/ ; --write saves results/LEADERBOARD.md . Challenge API hermes serve --config configs/ck26/prover.yaml --port 8000 GET /?question=...&dataset=<dataset id> returns {"dataset", "question", "query"} , the contract the official text2sparql-client calls, so any system can be submitted or scored with the organizers' tools. An unknown dataset is 404, a missing question 422. Source: serve.py . Rules for comparable numbers Set the official metrics on all items next to published entries, with strict and reproducible figures beside them. Never tune on the test benchmark; CK25 and CK26 share 49 of 50 queries. Keep benchmark content out of prompts and examples. A run with leak_gold or contaminated examples is an upper bound, not a result. Name the model. A local 8B model is a lower bound for a method, not its ceiling. Previous Evaluation Next Training-free

title: Training-free
text: hermes.systems.training_free Training-free The training-free system writes one SPARQL query from the schema vocabulary in a single model call, plus one repair call if the draft does not parse. On this page Command From Python Prompt Errors Command hermes generate \ --ontology GeoOutage.ttl \ --question "Which counties have the highest number of outages?" \ --context notes.txt \ --examples pairs.jsonl Flag Meaning --ontology , --graph , or --endpoint One is required: an RDF file, a graph name from data/graphs.yaml , or a SPARQL endpoint URL. --question Required. --context A text file of extra context. --examples JSONL, one object per line with nl and sparql ( nl_text and sparql_query are accepted). --system Any registered system; the default is training-free . Source: cli.py . From Python from hermes import Context, Example, TrainingFree system = TrainingFree() # or TrainingFree(llm=...) result = system( "Which counties have the highest number of outages?", "GeoOutage.ttl", Context(text="Counties are administrative regions.", examples=[Example(nl="List outage records.", sparql="SELECT ?rec WHERE { ?rec a geooutageonto:OutageRecord }")]), ) print(result["sparql"]) The result has sparql , model , and provider . Source: training_free.py . Prompt build_prompt joins these sections with a blank line: Instructions: one query, only the prefixes and terms below, match labels in quotes, triples inside WHERE , ORDER BY and LIMIT after it, no SELECT inside FILTER , do not copy the shape example, return only the query. A shape example with ex: terms that are not from the ontology. Prefixes, classes, and properties from the vocabulary . Context text and example pairs, when given. The question, last. Errors A reply without a query raises ValueError . A query that still fails to parse after one repair raises ValueError with the parser message. Model failures are LookupError ; see Models . Previous Experiments Next Vocabulary

title: Verified query planning over the SPARQL algebra
text: Verified query planning over the SPARQL algebra Hermes answers a question over a knowledge graph by planning a SPARQL query one algebra operator at a time. A verifier types every step against the RDF schema before it runs, and execution on the graph tells the planner what each step did. $ git clone https://github.com/lamng3/hermes.git && cd hermes $ pip install -e ".[dev]" $ hermes generate --graph corporate --system prover --question "..." The algebra Playground Benchmarks Four systems, one question recorded benchmark runs Try it: Pick a question, then switch systems to compare the SPARQL each one wrote and how it scored. Question Leaderboard set F-nDCG, ck26 Qwen3-14B on 100 questions of the Text2SPARQL 2026 corporate benchmark; answers are scored by the benchmark's official scorer. Several official systems score higher than every Hermes run, and the leaderboard shows them. The page computes nothing: it shows hermes/results/ck26 . This site documents the code of the paper Hermes: Verified Query Planning over the SPARQL Algebra with Language Agents (Lam Nguyen, Case Western Reserve University). The repository is its official implementation. The idea Language models usually write a whole SPARQL query, then repair it after it fails. A query optimizer works differently: it applies one algebraic operator at a time and estimates its effect before keeping it. Hermes takes the optimizer's view of query generation: A typed SPARQL algebra. A query plan is a term of the algebra. The RDF schema gives every variable a type, and rules decide without running the plan whether it is valid. See Verifier . Verified query planning. Actions are algebra operators. After each one the planner sees the number of solutions, how it changed, a sample of rows, and any error. A plan is accepted only when it is valid and meets a goal stated from the question. See Algebra . One interface for methods. One-shot generation, constraint-guided search (UniQGen), and the planners are swappable systems on the same graphs and the same scorer. See Systems . A reproducible evaluation. Six benchmarks in one format, and a scorer that reproduces every published Text2SPARQL 2026 score. See Benchmarks and Evaluation . The pieces Algebra Plans, actions, the explorer, and the feedback after every step. Verifier Typing, well-formedness, goals, and the prover system. Systems The registry and the four shipped systems. Graph stores Oxigraph, rdflib, and SPARQL endpoints behind one query call. Benchmarks Text2SPARQL and QALD in one normalized format, with caveats. Evaluation Official, strict, and reproducible-subset metrics. Experiments Configs, runs, the leaderboard, and the challenge API. Models Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible API, with retries and a replay cache. Quick start hermes data fetch ck26 # download and normalize a benchmark hermes run configs/ck26/algebra-agent.yaml # predict, execute, score hermes report # leaderboard with official peer scores One question at a time: hermes generate --graph corporate --system prover \ --question "Who is Heinrich Hoch's manager?" from hermes import KnowledgeGraph, ask kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_files("onto.ttl", "data.ttl") result = ask("Which cities hosted the Winter Olympics?", kg, system="prover") print(result["sparql"]) Install git clone https://github.com/lamng3/hermes.git cd hermes pip install -e ".[dev]" pytest The install name is hermes-sparql and the import name is hermes . Python 3.11 or newer. Dependencies are rdflib , pyoxigraph , httpx , and pyyaml . The tests need no model and no network.

title: Leaderboard
text: Results Leaderboard Every Hermes run next to the official systems of the Text2SPARQL 2026 challenge, ranked by the official scorer. Hermes is a research system, and it does not lead this board: the best official system scores well above every Hermes run on both tracks. The board shows that on purpose. It is useful for what it separates inside Hermes: the planner with a verifier ( prover ) beats the unverified algebra agent, which beats one-shot generation, and larger Qwen3 models help. How to read it Set F-nDCG is the challenge's headline metric: set F1 over the returned rows, combined with ranking quality. Hermes rows are runs of this repository (system and model in the name, @qwen3-14b for example). Official rows are the published scores of the challenge's other systems, shown for scale. LLM calls per item and GPU minutes are what a run cost; official systems report neither. Click a column to sort. Ranks stay with the set F-nDCG, so a sort does not change who is first. The numbers come from results/LEADERBOARD.md , which hermes report --write generates from every run's metrics.json ; see Experiments . Previous Benchmarks Next Evaluation

title: Models
text: hermes.llm Models Systems receive an LLM client, so experiments choose the model. Completions can be cached on disk, so a rerun replays the same outputs. On this page Clients Ollama OpenAI-compatible Cache and retries Clients from hermes import llm client = llm.create(provider="ollama", model="llama3.1", cache=".cache/llm") text = client.complete(prompt, system="...") Every client has complete(prompt, system) , model , and provider . llm.create builds one from a config's llm section; llm.from_env() builds the default from environment variables. Temperature is 0. Source: llm.py . Ollama Variable Default HERMES_OLLAMA_BASE_URL http://127.0.0.1:11434 HERMES_OLLAMA_MODEL chosen from installed models: llama3.1 , llama3 , mistral , phi3 , qwen2.5 , qwen , then the first installed The timeout is 180 seconds. Connection failures, timeouts, and missing models raise LookupError with the command to fix them. OpenAI-compatible Variable Default HERMES_LLM_PROVIDER set to openai to select this client HERMES_LLM_API_KEY required HERMES_LLM_BASE_URL https://api.together.xyz/v1 HERMES_LLM_MODEL meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-Turbo The timeout is 60 seconds. Cache and retries CachedLLM stores each completion as a JSON file keyed by a hash of the provider, model, system prompt, and prompt, and counts calls and cache hits for run.json . Both clients retry up to three attempts on read errors and on HTTP 429, 502, 503, and 504, with backoff. Previous Validation

title: Playground
text: Try it Playground Ask a question over the corporate knowledge graph, get a SPARQL query from a recorded Hermes system or from a model you run, and replay it one pattern at a time. On this page How to use it Why Oxigraph, and not OntoDB? What to expect from a small model What is not here What runs where Everything runs in your browser. The graph (about 26.6k triples of the Text2SPARQL corporate knowledge graph) is loaded into Oxigraph , a SPARQL engine compiled to WebAssembly. It is the engine Hermes itself uses for local graphs (through its Python binding, pyoxigraph ), so the answers are the ones Hermes's own runs would get. Hermes itself is Python and is not run here: the recorded queries are what its systems wrote with Qwen3-14B, and the model prompt is a port of the training-free system's. No model is hosted for this page, so Ask my model uses a model you run: Ollama on this computer is detected automatically, or you can load a tiny model that runs in your browser on WebGPU (a few hundred megabytes, kept by your browser), or point it at another endpoint. Loading the playground… How to use it Pick a sample question and press one of the recorded systems: the query it wrote appears, with its recorded score. Run it on the graph and compare what the systems wrote. The prover's query is loaded first. Press Replay step by step to add the query's patterns one at a time. After each, the solution count and its change show what a planner sees as it builds a plan, and a step that empties the result points at the wrong pattern. To use a model, open Your model , point it at an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (Ollama is the default), and press Ask my model . The prompt is the training-free system's; if the draft does not parse the page asks once to repair it, as that system does. Why Oxigraph, and not OntoDB? Hermes's default local store is Oxigraph (see Graph stores ), so the browser runs the same engine. OntoDB is not one of Hermes's stores, and it could not run Hermes's queries if it were: it answers only SELECT over a basic graph pattern with filters, and rejects OPTIONAL , UNION , property paths, and aggregates, while questions like "which bill of materials has the highest average unit cost" need aggregates. OntoDB is also a C++ engine that is not built for the web yet. What to expect from a small model Writing a query from this prompt is hard for small models. The tiny model that runs in your browser (LFM2.5 350M, in tests on 2026-10-22) produced a draft that did not parse, even after the one repair, for all eight sample questions, and the leaderboard shows the same trend: one-shot Qwen3-4B scores 0.000 and Qwen3-14B 0.090, against 0.282 for the best Hermes planner. Use Ollama with the largest model you have, and compare with the recorded queries above. For the in-browser model the page is mainly useful for seeing the pipeline cope: extraction, one repair, then a plain report of the failure. What is not here The typed algebra and the verifier are not run in the browser. The replay shows the planner's feedback (solutions and their change), not its type checks; see Verifier . Answers are not scored here. The scores shown for recorded queries come from the benchmark's official scorer, as in the leaderboard . Previous Overview Next Algebra

title: Stages
text: hermes.stages Stages apply_stages walks a fixed tuple. Each function takes the draft and returns a query. Replacing a function is how a later technique enters the training-free pipeline. On this page Contract Guardrails Query guided, context guided, chase and backchase Contract def stage(sparql, *, ontology, context): return sparql STAGES = (guardrails, query_guided, context_guided, chase_backchase) ontology is the vocabulary dict, not a path. The stages run on the first draft and again on the repair draft. Source: stages.py . Guardrails Declares known prefixes that the draft uses but does not declare, from the vocabulary and the RDF, RDFS, OWL, and XSD namespaces. Prefixes inside IRIs and string literals are ignored. Rejecting terms outside the vocabulary is the job of the verifier , which the planners use. Query guided, context guided, chase and backchase later These return the draft unchanged. Chase and Backchase now lives in the uniqgen system, over constraint tables, rather than as a post-processing stage. Previous Vocabulary Next Validation

title: Graph stores
text: hermes.store, hermes.knowledge, hermes.linking Graph stores Systems and the scorer only call query(sparql), which returns SPARQL 1.1 JSON results. The same system runs on local files or a remote endpoint. On this page KnowledgeGraph Stores Entity linking KnowledgeGraph from hermes import KnowledgeGraph kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_files("prod-vocab.ttl", "prod-inst.ttl") # Oxigraph kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_files("onto.ttl", engine="rdflib") kg = KnowledgeGraph.from_endpoint("https://dbpedia.org/sparql", prefixes=[("dbo", "http://dbpedia.org/ontology/")]) A knowledge graph pairs a store with the vocabulary used to prompt for it. schema names smaller files to read the vocabulary from. Loading is lazy, so nothing is parsed until the first query. kg.executions counts real executions. Source: knowledge.py . Stores Store Backend OxigraphStore Local RDF files in Oxigraph. The default: it loads the 26.6k-triple corporate graph in a fraction of a second. LocalStore Local RDF files in rdflib, in pure Python. EndpointStore A SPARQL endpoint over HTTP POST, with retries on server errors, a 60-second timeout, and a User-Agent header. CachedStore Wraps any store, memoizes results, and counts executions. A failed query raises QueryError ; try_query returns empty results instead. Turtle, N-Triples, N-Quads, RDF/XML, and TriG are read by extension. Source: store.py . Entity linking LabelIndex reads rdfs:label , skos:prefLabel , skos:altLabel , and the local names of typed subjects once, and matches in memory, falling back to partial-word matches. ExactLabel sends capitalized n-grams of the question to the store as label literals in one VALUES query, for large endpoints such as DBpedia. linker_for(kg) picks the first for local stores and the second for endpoints. Source: linking.py . Previous Systems Next Benchmarks

title: Systems
text: hermes.systems Systems A system turns a question into SPARQL over a knowledge graph. Systems register by name, so experiments swap them without code changes. On this page Contract Shipped systems Register a system Plugins Contract def system(question, kg, context): return {"sparql": "..."} kg is a KnowledgeGraph . context is a Context or None : free text, example question and query pairs, and, for ablations only, reference answers. The result has at least sparql ; systems may add traces and counters. hermes.ask(question, kg_or_path, context, system=..., **params) runs one. Source: systems/__init__.py . Shipped systems Name Method Parameters training-free One prompted draft, fixed stages, one repair. Details . llm uniqgen UniQGen (Wang et al., arXiv:2605.00845 ): a constraint table, then Chase and Backchase against reference answers. beam_width 5, max_depth 5, threshold 1.0, alpha 0.5, hops 2, oracle (LLM, "gold" , or a callable), llm algebra-agent An LLM plans over the algebra with execution feedback. max_steps 15, sample_size 5, max_entities 10, llm prover The algebra agent with the verifier and goals. as algebra-agent The UniQGen reimplementation differs from the paper in two documented ways: queries are rendered from constraints deterministically, and candidates are scored by comparing answer sets with the reference answers. That keeps it at two model calls per question. Aggregates, ORDER BY , and LIMIT are not handled. Register a system import hermes @hermes.systems.register("my-system") class MySystem: def __init__(self, llm=None, depth=3): # config params arrive here self.llm = llm def __call__(self, question, kg, context): return {"sparql": "SELECT * WHERE { ?s ?p ?o } LIMIT 1"} A class receives its parameters from systems.create(name, **params) , which is how experiment configs pass them; a function takes none. A name can be registered once. hermes.systems.available() lists the names, and hermes systems prints them. Plugins Another package can add a system without touching Hermes by declaring an entry point in the hermes.systems group that points at the system. Previous Verifier Next Graph stores

title: Validation
text: hermes.validate Validation prepare_draft extracts a query and moves solution modifiers out of WHERE. parse_error checks it with rdflib. One repair call is allowed. On this page Extract Lift modifiers Parse and repair Extract extract_sparql prefers the first fenced block, including a sparql fence, and keeps the first span that starts at SELECT , ASK , CONSTRUCT , or DESCRIBE with any PREFIX lines before it. An empty result raises ValueError . Lift modifiers Models often write ORDER BY , LIMIT , GROUP BY , HAVING , or OFFSET inside the outer WHERE block. lift_modifiers moves those lines after the block when they sit at brace depth zero; modifiers inside a nested SELECT stay put. Parse and repair parse_error calls rdflib.plugins.sparql.prepareQuery and returns None or the parser message. On an error, the training-free system sends repair_prompt once, then runs extraction and the stages again. A second error raises ValueError . Source: validate.py . Previous Stages Next Models

title: Verifier
text: hermes.kernel Verifier The verifier checks a plan against the schema and a stated goal before anything runs. Ill-typed steps never reach the graph store. On this page Typing Errors Goals The prover system Typing Schema.from_kg(kg) reads classes, properties, rdfs:domain , rdfs:range , and the closure of rdfs:subClassOf . Kernel.check(plan, goal) builds a typing context for the plan's variables: ?x a C gives ?x : C . ?x p ?y gives ?x the domain of p and ?y its range. Classes are compared up to subclass. Two unrelated classes on one variable are a warning, not an error: RDF is open world and the schema need not declare disjointness. Source: kernel.py . Errors Error Example message Unknown term in a namespace the schema describes unknown property ex:hosts (did you mean ex:hosted?) Literal where an entity is required type mismatch: ex:hosted expects an entity of ex:OlympicGames, got the literal "Winter" Literal used as an entity, or the reverse type mismatch: ?s is a literal but ... Unbound variable unbound variable ?y in FILTER BIND onto a bound variable BIND target ?g is already bound Ungrouped projection ?g is neither grouped nor aggregated Variables that occur only inside MINUS are not bound, as in SPARQL. The check runs in one pass over the plan; nothing is executed. Goals A goal states what the question asks for before the query exists: {"op": "goal", "answer": ["?c"], "kind": "entity", "type": "ex:City", "many": true} kind is entity , literal , number , or boolean ; type is optional; many is false when one answer is expected. The verifier lists the open goals the plan does not yet meet: the answer variable is not bound or not projected, other variables are projected, a number is not an aggregate or a numeric value, an entity is a literal, the type is not established, a yes-or-no question is not an ASK , or, after execution, there is more than one solution when one was asked for. The goal is written by the planner from the question, so it can be wrong. The verifier guarantees that a plan has the shape its goal asks for, not that the goal is the question. The prover system prover is the algebra agent with the verifier installed. The planner states the goal first. Each turn the prompt shows the plan state: the typing context and the open goals. finish is refused while an error or an open goal remains. The result adds kernel_rejections and goal . Source: prover.py . context: ?c : ex:City ?g : ex:OlympicGames open goals: goals accomplished Previous Algebra Next Systems

title: Vocabulary
text: hermes.ontology Vocabulary The vocabulary is a compact list of prefixes, classes, and properties. It is queried through a store, so it works the same for a file and an endpoint. On this page Result Classes and properties Prefixes Result kg.vocabulary { "classes": ['ex:City "City"'], "properties": ['ex:inCountry "in country"'], "prefixes": [("ex", "http://example.org/demo#")], } vocabulary(store, declared, limit) runs two queries on the store; load_vocabulary(path) does the same for one file. Source: ontology.py . Classes and properties Classes are IRIs typed owl:Class or rdfs:Class . Properties are IRIs typed owl:ObjectProperty , owl:DatatypeProperty , or rdf:Property . An rdfs:label is appended in quotes. Each list stops at vocabulary_limit terms (60 by default). A limit of 0 skips the queries, which is how large graphs such as DBpedia and Wikidata are declared in data/graphs.yaml . Prefixes For files, declared prefixes come from the @prefix lines in the file text; for endpoints, from the graph's entry in data/graphs.yaml . RDF, RDFS, OWL, XSD, and XML namespaces are skipped, and at most 12 prefixes are kept. A namespace without a declaration gets a prefix from its last path segment, with a numeric suffix on collision. Previous Training-free Next Stages
